item.title: From Bury to AC Milan: Bournemouth's journey to 'dreamland'
item.description: Bournemouth play AC Milan 15 years to the day they lost at home to Bury in League One [Getty Images] "I'm pinching myself," says Bournemouth fan Kirk Tovey. "It's not long ago we were playing Oldham Athletic and Hartlepool United in League One. Now I'm about to watch us play AC Milan. "It's absolute madness." Fifteen years to the day after Bournemouth lost 2-1 at home to Bury in the third tier of English football, the Cherries host seven-time champions of Europe AC Milan in the Europa League on Thursday (20:00 BST). It is a game between the club that refused to die against the 11-time European Cup finalists on what promises to be a momentous night in the history of the 127-year-old Dorset club. "Over the last decade, my hometown club has achieved dreamland," Tony Pulis, who played in Bournemouth's defence before managing them from 1992-94 and still lives in the area, tells BBC Sport. "It's an unbelievable story, when I think back to what the club was like when I was player, coach and then manager there in the 1980s and early 1990s, but one that hopefully just keeps going." Bournemouth's troubled past and their subsequent climb up the leagues is well documented - from bucket collections and facing liquidation as recently as 2008 to finishing 21st in League Two in 2008-09 and winning promotion to the Premier League in 2015. Now an established top-flight side, Bournemouth are making their debut season in Europe, looking to topple one of European football's great clubs. "We used to train on the park over from the stadium," says Joe Partington, who played in midfield for Bournemouth in League One and League Two after coming through the academy, and is now BBC Radio Solent's regular Cherries summariser. "Now fans walk through the park to watch European games." Minus 17 to European dreams as Bournemouth fairytale continues 'The whole thing still seems surreal for fans' AC Milan's last Champions League triumph came in 2007 when they beat Liverpool in the final in Athens [Getty Images] Hottest ticket in town On this day in 2011, Bournemouth were 21st in the third tier of English football, with 12 points from 14 games, after losing at home to Bury. Later on that season, they would lose away at Bury, Rochdale and Oldham. "Back then, we had to get changed in one part of Bournemouth then drive somewhere else to train before driving somewhere else for lunch," says Partington, who featured in that game against Bury 15 years ago. Tovey, from the Cherries Red Army fan channel, recalls home crowds of 6,000 around that time. "As a fan, you could just rock up 10 minutes before kick-off and walk in," he says. Not any more. While Bournemouth's Vitality stadium is comfortably the smallest in the Premier League in terms of capacity, work is under way to expand it and last week's attendance figure of 12,070 for the 3-0 Europa League win over Sturm Graz was easily their highest of the 21st century. item.content:encoded: Bournemouth play AC Milan 15 years to the day they lost at home to Bury in League One [Getty Images] "I'm pinching myself," says Bournemouth fan Kirk Tovey. "It's not long ago we were playing Oldham Athletic and Hartlepool United in League One. Now I'm about to watch us play AC Milan. "It's absolute madness." Fifteen years to the day after Bournemouth lost 2-1 at home to Bury in the third tier of English football, the Cherries host seven-time champions of Europe AC Milan in the Europa League on Thursday (20:00 BST). It is a game between the club that refused to die against the 11-time European Cup finalists on what promises to be a momentous night in the history of the 127-year-old Dorset club. "Over the last decade, my hometown club has achieved dreamland," Tony Pulis, who played in Bournemouth's defence before managing them from 1992-94 and still lives in the area, tells BBC Sport. "It's an unbelievable story, when I think back to what the club was like when I was player, coach and then manager there in the 1980s and early 1990s, but one that hopefully just keeps going." Bournemouth's troubled past and their subsequent climb up the leagues is well documented - from bucket collections and facing liquidation as recently as 2008 to finishing 21st in League Two in 2008-09 and winning promotion to the Premier League in 2015. Now an established top-flight side, Bournemouth are making their debut season in Europe, looking to topple one of European football's great clubs. "We used to train on the park over from the stadium," says Joe Partington, who played in midfield for Bournemouth in League One and League Two after coming through the academy, and is now BBC Radio Solent's regular Cherries summariser. "Now fans walk through the park to watch European games." Minus 17 to European dreams as Bournemouth fairytale continues 'The whole thing still seems surreal for fans' AC Milan's last Champions League triumph came in 2007 when they beat Liverpool in the final in Athens [Getty Images] Hottest ticket in town On this day in 2011, Bournemouth were 21st in the third tier of English football, with 12 points from 14 games, after losing at home to Bury. Later on that season, they would lose away at Bury, Rochdale and Oldham. "Back then, we had to get changed in one part of Bournemouth then drive somewhere else to train before driving somewhere else for lunch," says Partington, who featured in that game against Bury 15 years ago. Tovey, from the Cherries Red Army fan channel, recalls home crowds of 6,000 around that time. "As a fan, you could just rock up 10 minutes before kick-off and walk in," he says. Not any more. While Bournemouth's Vitality stadium is comfortably the smallest in the Premier League in terms of capacity, work is under way to expand it and last week's attendance figure of 12,070 for the 3-0 Europa League win over Sturm Graz was easily their highest of the 21st century. Another 12,000-plus will pack in for the visit of an AC Milan team managed by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim, with many fans resigned to watching the match on television after missing out on a ticket. "My niece loves Bournemouth but she's missed out because she hasn't got enough points to get a ticket," adds Tovey. "She's gutted." Pulis has been impressed with the club's significant progress under the ownership of US billionaire Bill Foley, who completed his takeover in 2022. "They are now an established Premier League club, with a brand new training facility that can rival most in this country," he says. "A top-class academy facility for the boys and girls and a group of first-team players that not only play but run themselves into the ground every game." Bournemouth fan Kirk Tovey (right) with his son Owen outside Bournemouth's ground [BBC] 'Wow factor' AC Milan are fourth in Serie A on 15 points from seven games, four points behind leaders and arch-rivals Inter Milan. It is 19 years since they were last crowned champions of Europe and four years since they won the last of their 19 Serie A titles. "They are not the team they used to be," says Tovey. "This is not the AC Milan of Kaka, Alessandro Nesta, Paolo Maldini, Filippo Inzaghi or Clarence Seedorf. But they are still seven-time champions of Europe and they are a massive football club. "When the draw came out and you looked at the eight teams we were drawn against, AC Milan was the one everyone went 'wow'." Bournemouth, who have won both their opening Europa League games, have hosted European royalty before. Cristiano Ronaldo was the world's most expensive footballer when he scored two goals in Real Madrid's 6-0 pre-season win over the Cherries in 2013 - the club called this a "celebratory exhibition match" after winning promotion to the Championship. Lining up against Bournemouth that day was Luka Modric, who is expected to feature on Thursday at the age of 41. Modric, a six-time Champions League winner with Real, has started five matches for AC Milan this season. "I would love him to be on the pitch so we can say we have seen Modric in a competitive game at Dean Court [Vitality stadium]," Bournemouth fan Chris told BBC Radio 5 Live's 606 football phone-in. 'We've earned the right to play AC Milan' This is not be the first time AC Milan have visited Bournemouth. In 2016, the Rossoneri sent a team to play in a testimonial for long-serving Cherries defender Warren Cummings. Thursday's match is different. "It's not a charity game or a pre-season friendly," says Partington. "It's Bournemouth against AC Milan in a competitive European match. "People are gobsmacked that this is now a normal thing." Bournemouth and AC Milan also share the same colours. When John Bond was manager of Bournemouth in the early 1970s, he changed their traditional cherry-red shirts to red and black stripes in a nod to Milan's dominance on the continent during the 1960s. In another homage to Thursday's illustrious opposition, the club changed its name in 1972 from Bournemouth and Boscombe Athletic to AFC Bournemouth, in an attempt to sound more continental, while taking them to the top of the alphabetical list of League clubs above Arsenal. "The fact that Bournemouth were inspired by AC Milan shows how big the club is and the history of it," former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who joined the Italian club in 2023, tells BBC Radio Solent. "AC Milan have inspired people to watch football and love football." England international Loftus-Cheek adds: "Bournemouth belong in the Premier League and now they're playing in Europe and get a chance to play AC Milan. It's a great spectacle for the fans." The Cherries and AC Milan might be poles apart in terms of European experience but they are much closer when it comes to recent form. "We have earned the right to be in the Europa League through hard work and ambition," says Tovey. "We might be little old Bournemouth but we absolutely deserve to be playing AC Milan." item.title: ‘The Angel Reese Effect,’ ‘They Said Nobody Watches Unless Caitlin (Clark) Is Playing’ — WNBA World Buzzes As Finals Opener Sets Viewership Record
item.description: The WNBA Finals opener drew a record 2.1 million viewers, sparking fan reactions about Angel Reese and Caitlin Clark. Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries became the most-watched Finals opener in league history. The game averaged 2.1 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, prompting some to credit Angel Reese while others compared the numbers to games featuring Caitlin Clark. WNBA Fans Credit Angel Reese, Debate Caitlin Clark’s Impact After Record Finals Opener The historic audience revived a familiar discussion about Reese’s and Clark’s respective roles in drawing viewers to the WNBA. Some saw the numbers as support for Reese’s past comments that the league’s popularity isn’t dependent on one player. “Angel Reese rn after saying ‘People watch because of me too, not one person,’ two years ago,” one X user posted. Another viewer challenged the idea that Clark was necessary to attract a large audience. “The Angel Reese effect! They said nobody watches the WNBA unless Caitlin is playing 😂,” the fan commented . Others focused on how the audience compared with previous broadcasts. “Agreed. 2.1M is a great start for Game 1 up against college football. It’ll be interesting to see if the next few games of the WNBA Finals can reach or beat some of the better viewership numbers this season,” columnist Christine Brennan wrote . Reporter Dan Zaksheske offered a different perspective on the viewership figures. “Game 1 of the WNBA Finals averaged 2.1 million viewers, which is a great number for the WNBA. It was the league’s 11th most-watched game this season. All 10 games ahead of it featured the Indiana Fever,” Zaksheske tweeted . One viewer pushed back against turning the ratings discussion into a competition between players. “Yes, there have been other more watched games, but that’s far from the point people. No need to pin different women against each other and just watch it or don’t watch. The WNBA is seeing big jumps of not just viewership but in talent. Fan how you want but don’t let your hate for something prevent you from seeing the facts and reasoning,” the user wrote . The Atlantic’s Jemele Hill also reacted with an emoji. Fever writer Robin Lundberg provided additional context on ratings. Last year’s Finals opener between the Las Vegas Aces and Phoenix Mercury averaged 1.9 million viewers on ESPN, while the four-game series averaged 1.5 million. This year’s opener also fell short of the 2.25 million viewers who watched Game 3 of the first-round series between the Aces and Fever. The Dream and Valkyries entered the Finals seeking their first championships. Atlanta previously reached the championship round three times between 2010 and 2013, while Golden State made its first appearance in just its second season. Saturday’s opener featured seven lead changes and six ties. Neither team led by double digits, and the Valkyries came away with a 68-64 victory. SEE ALSO: ‘I Don’t Know Who’s Mentally Strong Enough’ —

SEE ALSO: ‘I Don’t Know Who’s Mentally Strong Enough’ — 2-Time WNBA Champion Questions Valkyries’ Solution To Handle Angel Reese Allisha Gray led Atlanta with 19 points on 5-for-19 shooting, including 1-for-8 from 3-point range. Reese finished with 14 points and 12 rebounds but did not make a field goal in the second half. Gabby Williams led Golden State with 26 points and was the team’s only double-digit scorer. Kiah Stokes added 9 points. Game 3 on Wednesday coincided with an 11-game NBA schedule, giving the Finals additional competition for viewers. item.title: Club ready to do 'everything possible' to sign Liverpool legend
item.description: Club ready to do 'everything possible' to sign Liverpool legend Liverpool are likely to go through some massive changes over the next year or so. Because, by June 2027, at least a handful of the Reds' first-team squad will be out of contract. And, while this wouldn't ordinarily be a problem, the fact that some of Liverpool's best players are part of that group is massively worrying. Liverpool's backroom staff all know how important these players are to the Anfield outfit but, that clearly doesn't mean anything as negotiations for new deals haven't commenced yet. This has caused the rumour mill to go into overdrive with some players already being linked with new clubs. Flamengo want to sign Alisson from Liverpool Alisson is one of the many players who look likely to leave Liverpool for free this summer. As much as Liverpool won't want him to go, at the moment, everything is pointing in that direction. The Reds extended his contract by a year last season and, although no negotiations needed to be held due to the option to extend that Liverpool had, you'd have expected them to try and keep him tied down for a little longer. He may be 34 years old now but, he's still easily one of the best goalkeepers in the world . Admittedly, his injury history leaves a lot to be desired but, if he figures out a way to keep on top of that, he could play at the top level for many more years. But, since his contract is set to expire and Liverpool haven't entered negotiations with him yet, other clubs have started to show an interest in signing him with 1News Brazil now sharing that Flamengo are keen on adding him to their squad. "Flamengo is keeping Liverpool's Alisson Becker as a name that could influence the club's future planning," they wrote . "According to this journalist's sources, if the goalkeeper decides to return to Brazilian football, Flamengo intends to do everything possible to make his signing a reality. "The potential arrival of the number 1 goalkeeper would be a high-impact move in the transfer market. "With international experience and notable spells with the Brazilian national team, Alisson possesses characteristics that make him capable of raising the level of the Flamengo squad. "However, the player's desire to return to Brazil would be crucial for any initiative to move forward." item.content:encoded: Club ready to do 'everything possible' to sign Liverpool legend Liverpool are likely to go through some massive changes over the next year or so. Because, by June 2027, at least a handful of the Reds' first-team squad will be out of contract. Admittedly, his injury history leaves a lot to be desired but, if he figures out a way to keep on top of that, he could play at the top level for many more years. But, since his contract is set to expire and Liverpool haven't entered negotiations with him yet, other clubs have started to show an interest in signing him with 1News Brazil now sharing that Flamengo are keen on adding him to their squad. "Flamengo is keeping Liverpool's Alisson Becker as a name that could influence the club's future planning," they wrote . "According to this journalist's sources, if the goalkeeper decides to return to Brazilian football, Flamengo intends to do everything possible to make his signing a reality. "The potential arrival of the number 1 goalkeeper would be a high-impact move in the transfer market. "With international experience and notable spells with the Brazilian national team, Alisson possesses characteristics that make him capable of raising the level of the Flamengo squad. His distribution was well-below par and, his shot-stopping, something that he was high regarded for across the world, just stopped happening. Of course, he may have to if Alisson ends up injured but, for now, the Brazilian's fitness levels seem fairly high. And, since he's likely to play an important role throughout the rest of the current campaign, there's really no reason for Liverpool to not extend his stay. That is, especially if they want to get back to their best and start winning trophies again.

item.title: 0 duels won, 50% aerial battles won, 1 clearance: Returning Matthijs de Ligt brutally left hung out to dry by INEOS’ failings
item.description: 0 duels won, 50% aerial battles won, 1 clearance: Returning Matthijs de Ligt brutally left hung out to dry by INEOS’ failings Manchester United were ruthlessly taken apart 4-1 by Como in rainy northern Italy on Wednesday evening. The match It was a chastening event and demonstrated to all of Europe how far the club has fallen. United were outclassed all over the pitch and can probably count themselves fortunate to have only lost by three, as Cesc Fabregas masterminded a famous victory for the Serie A club. Matthijs de Ligt The Dutch centre back has not played since last November but had to fill in today due to United’s crippling defensive injuries. Leny Yoro was suspended, and Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven were both injured for the game. This meant De Ligt had to start alongside Harry Maguire , and the two never looked comfortable together. The former Bayern Munich defender was at sixes and sevens for Como’s second goal when he lost his man and Anastasios Douvika raced in to give the home side the lead. In 79 minutes of action, De Ligt only managed two defensive actions : one clearance and one interception on the night. He did not block any shots and, incredibly, did not even compete in a ground duel—something very unusual for the usually commanding and duel-loving centre back. The centre back also only competed in two aerial battles, winning one. His passing was accurate, completing 92% of his attempts, but they were not dangerous as he did not complete any key passes. Analysis It seems harsh to blame De Ligt for such a poor showing, as he should never have been thrown in at the deep end like he was, especially with such an ill-fitting partner as Maguire. Nonetheless, it demonstrates the sad state of affairs the club is in that their squad is so weak they must face a Champions League encounter in this scenario. Matthijs de Ligt career stats Featured image by Marco Luzzani via Getty Images online polls

He did not block any shots and, incredibly, did not even compete in a ground duel—something very unusual for the usually commanding and duel-loving centre back. The centre back also only competed in two aerial battles, winning one. His passing was accurate, completing 92% of his attempts, but they were not dangerous as he did not complete any key passes. Analysis It seems harsh to blame De Ligt for such a poor showing, as he should never have been thrown in at the deep end like he was, especially with such an ill-fitting partner as Maguire. Nonetheless, it demonstrates the sad state of affairs the club is in that their squad is so weak they must face a Champions League encounter in this scenario. item.title: Team England athlete teaches the art of falling over
item.description: Team England athlete Kelly Petersen-Pollard has been leading a session in Lichfield [BBC] A Team England athlete has been leading a judo session in Lichfield, teaching people with mobility issues the art of falling over safely. Judo champion Kelly Petersen-Pollard hosted a class at MoveMojo's Centre in Lichfield, Staffordshire, on Tuesday. About a third of people aged 65 and over, and about half of people aged 80 and over, fall at least once per year, according to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE). Petersen-Pollard said: "We're basically going around and teaching people to fall so that when falls do happen, you can land a lot better to prevent injuries - especially when you're getting older and stuff like that." Judo champion Kelly Peterson-Pollard helped people in Hammerwich, Staffordshire, on Tuesday Petersen-Pollard said people had to learn to "fall well" in judo and they were taught techniques to make it less painful – including both forwards and backwards break falls. "I guess if you learn how to do it the judo way - which you might not think you're going to do that as you're mid-fall, but it might come back in your memory and you will put your arm out or something like that," she said. "You kind of use the softer side of your arm to hit the ground – so if you're going backwards, you'll smack the floor which will then take the pressure off where you're going to fall, so straight onto your back otherwise." Tracy Rhodes is waiting for a knee replacement operation. She took part in the session and said it will help build her confidence. She added: "I'm prone to falls at the moment, so starting to learn how to fall is really good. [It's] stuff I can practice at home." Judo participants are taught how to fall safely, a skill that can be applied to those in later life as well [BBC] As well as sessions to teach older people how to fall, there were other sessions being organised for children who have learning disabilities. "It's all about bringing different people from the community all together with Team England athletes, and letting them see what judo is all about," Petersen-Pollard said. She added judo was a sport "anyone can do" and was fun to join in with. "I think some people haven't heard of judo, or if they have they think 'oh, I can't do that, that's too hard'," she said. "There's so many things in judo that aren't just the competitive, elite side." She added that it also helps to bring shy people out of their shell and helped them to meet new people. Follow BBC Stoke & Staffordshire on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . item.title: The Necessary Spark: Cole Knuble Is Injecting Life Into the Flyers Lineup
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Not a lot of brain cells,” said Flyers forward Trevor Zegras following Monday’s win vs. the Colorado Avalanche, about the trio of Denver Barkery, Alex Bump , and Cole Knuble . “They’re great; they bring a lot of energy for the team in the locker room and on the bench. They’re having a blast, which goes up and down the lineup.” The Flyers have felt the youthful energy after a recent flurry of call-ups, including Bump’s return from the AHL and Knuble’s call-up and NHL debut. After a sluggish start to the 2026-27 season, the Flyers signed veteran winger Michael Bunting , looking to provide a spark. Bunting has looked solid so far in his time in Philly, but he has not found the offensive production that the Flyers were hoping for. That spark was still missing. The Flyers found that spark with their new wave of young guys, and Cole Knuble is leading that charge. Knuble scored not his first, but his first two career NHL goals on Wednesday against the Buffalo Sabres en route to their 3-1 win over the Atlantic Division foe. “[I’m] so excited for the kid, you know, and then (Knuble) getting another one,” said head coach Rick Tocchet on Cole Knuble scoring his first two NHL goals. “I think we all know he had a really good training camp; he stuck with it, went down [to the AHL]. Great attitude. And obviously, good things are happening for him. Even if he was held off the scoresheet on Monday, Knuble’s impact was on display against the Avalanche with his energy and hustle. He was rewarded with his first taste and a double dip of NHL scoring on Wednesday. Knuble was called up on Monday due to a lack of healthy forwards. It may not have been intended to find the spark. But that is exactly what happened. Cole Knuble on His 2 Games With the Flyers, So Far “I’ve felt better and better every period,” said Knuble on his first taste of NHL action after Wednesday’s win. “So, I think it’ll continue to come. It’ll be nice to get some practice time. You know, maybe start playing with the same players . I think it’ll just get better and better.” “I think I can obviously play and help the team at this level,” said Knuble. “I think I can bring energy, and I’ll do whatever it takes to be a part of this group.” In his short two-game stint with the Flyers so far, he has done just that. NHL Game Score Impact Card for Philadelphia Flyers on 2026-10-21: pic.twitter.com/TQK3LXTMQA — HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) October 22, 2026 He’s making his impact on the team, producing offense, and bringing a spark to the team’s 4th line. When asked about his early success, the young Flyers’ winger says the work he’s put in has helped him get here. “I’ve put a lot of work in over the years; I’m confident in my abilities. It’s obviously a jump up. The best players in the world. I play with really great teammates too. So obviously those guys have been great for me. “ Read More: Cole Knuble Scores First Two NHL Goals in Flyers Win vs. Sabre Read more at Ph

item.title: Tyrese Haliburton, Derik Queen have to be separated after verbal altercation in Pacers-Pelicans
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Tyrese Haliburton, Derik Queen have to be separated after verbal altercation in Pacers-Pelicans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indiana Pacers and the New Orleans Pelicans battled in a seesaw affair in their season opener at Smoothie King Center on Wednesday. The Pacers went on a surge in the fourth quarter and pulled off a come-from-behind win, 123-120. Tyrese Haliburton was terrific in his much-awaited return from his Achilles injury, finishing with 23 points on 8-of-15 shooting and 12 assists. Haliburton scored eight of Indiana’s 10 points in a 90-second stretch in the final period to seize control. The two-time All-Star also had a heated exchange with Derik Queen as they were walking to their respective benches in the fourth quarter. They were separated before anything escalated. Haliburton was called for a technical foul. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tyrese Haliburton was given a technical foul for this altercation involving Derik Queen 👀 pic.twitter.com/WdgE8mypO2 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 22, 2026 Queen had a solid outing with 10 points, 10 rebounds, and two steals in 18 minutes off the bench. He is expected to take the next step after showing promise in his rookie year. The 21-year-old Queen has a sense of humor and a fun-loving personality , but he showed that he will never back down when he is on the floor, even against an established veteran like Haliburton. Haliburton had plenty of support, with Pascal Siakam tallying 30 points and eight rebounds and Ivica Zubac adding 16 points, 25 rebounds, and two blocks. Dejounte Murray led the Pelicans with 23 points, three rebounds, seven assists, two steals, and three blocks. Zion Williamson contributed 22 points, three rebounds, three assists, and three steals. Indiana outscored New Orleans, 37-28, in the fourth quarter. The Pacers and the Pelicans will return to action on Friday against the Milwaukee Bucks and the Utah Jazz, respectively. Related: NBA stars Paolo Banchero, Jalen Johnson have to be seperated after tense end to Hawks-Magic Related: Is Mavericks’ Dereck Lively II ready for season opener vs. Rockets after missing most of last season with injury?

item.title: Man United’s latest shambolic performance leaves Michael Carrick on the brink
item.description: The saying goes that a picture is worth a thousand words, and in some ways the photos of Michael Carrick on the pitch in Como may tell you more than a match report ever could. United have had many a night to forget in recent seasons, but a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League goes down as one of the worst in living memory. In fact the Italian minnows, taking part in Europe’s premier competition for the first time, put United to the sword in a second-half performance that could well cost Carrick his job. Michael Carrick endured another tough evening as Man United boss (Reuters) And held his hands up in apology to United fans at the end of the match (PA) The fact that Cesc Fabregas – a man who has been touted as Carrick’s successor – delivered this chastening defeat is all the more intriguing. United conceded within 47 seconds in a dispiriting defeat to Atletico Madrid last week and they just about managed better on the shores of Lake Como, although barely... Man of the match Nico Paz curled in a superb effort within two minutes to put the hosts ahead. In hindsight it set the tone for the evening, though even the most pessimistic United player could not have imagined the embarrassment they were about to endure. Carrick’s side managed to settle despite conceding so early last week, but they were all over the place during a wet and windy start in Como, with the hosts threatening twice more within the opening 15 minutes before Harry Maguire flashed a header wide. A superb curled effort from Nico Paz opened the scoring within two minutes (Reuters) That half-chance was to be United’s best opening, at least until after the game had completely got away from them. Como continued to have the best chances, with Tasos Douvikas forcing Senne Lammens into a save before blasting over from inside the area a few minutes later. Shouts of ‘attack, attack, attack’ in the 34th minute summed up the United display, though a flash of the stats board in the 37th minute showed Como had completed 307 passes to United’s 172, with three shots on target to zero and 62 per cent possession. This was more than just an off-day. Possession may not be nine-tenths of the law in football anymore , but this was still an embarrassing showing from the visiting side. United were outplayed by Como in every department in the first half and they could barely get near them in midfield at times; when they did get the ball, they quickly looked out of ideas in possession too. This was not possession that was deliberately ceded, but rather possession that could not be won in the first place. United were poor from start to finish as they failed to compete with the hosts (Getty) Carrick clearly identified something was wrong, though he waited until half-time to make his two changes. It did not have the desired effect. Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo were brought on at the break to try and lift United but the visitors instead found themselves two goals behind within five minutes of the second half
item.content:encoded: The saying goes that a picture is worth a thousand words, and in some ways the photos of Michael Carrick on the pitch in Como may tell you more than a match report ever could. United have had many a night to forget in recent seasons, but a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League goes down as one of the worst in living memory. In fact the Italian minnows, taking part in Europe’s premier competition for the first time, put United to the sword in a second-half performance that could well cost Carrick his job. Michael Carrick endured another tough evening as Man United boss (Reuters) And held his hands up in apology to United fans at the end of the match (PA) The fact that Cesc Fabregas – a man who has been touted as Carrick’s successor – delivered this chastening defeat is all the more intriguing. United conceded within 47 seconds in a dispiriting defeat to Atletico Madrid last week and they just about managed better on the shores of Lake Como, although barely... Man of the match Nico Paz curled in a superb effort within two minutes to put the hosts ahead. In hindsight it set the tone for the evening, though even the most pessimistic United player could not have imagined the embarrassment they were about to endure. Carrick’s side managed to settle despite conceding so early last week, but they were all over the place during a wet and windy start in Como, with the hosts threatening twice more within the opening 15 minutes before Harry Maguire flashed a header wide. A superb curled effort from Nico Paz opened the scoring within two minutes (Reuters) That half-chance was to be United’s best opening, at least until after the game had completely got away from them. Como continued to have the best chances, with Tasos Douvikas forcing Senne Lammens into a save before blasting over from inside the area a few minutes later. Shouts of ‘attack, attack, attack’ in the 34th minute summed up the United display, though a flash of the stats board in the 37th minute showed Como had completed 307 passes to United’s 172, with three shots on target to zero and 62 per cent possession. This was more than just an off-day. Possession may not be nine-tenths of the law in football anymore , but this was still an embarrassing showing from the visiting side. United were outplayed by Como in every department in the first half and they could barely get near them in midfield at times; when they did get the ball, they quickly looked out of ideas in possession too. This was not possession that was deliberately ceded, but rather possession that could not be won in the first place. United were poor from start to finish as they failed to compete with the hosts (Getty) Carrick clearly identified something was wrong, though he waited until half-time to make his two changes. It did not have the desired effect. Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo were brought on at the break to try and lift United but the visitors instead found themselves two goals behind within five minutes of the second half starting, with the electric Paz slipping a through ball into the path of Douvikas to leave the Greek striker with a simple finish lifted past Lammens. It was no less than Como deserved but the game still did not feel like it had completely escaped the visitors, even if they had put in an abject performance leading up to it. In fact, United’s first real spell of pressure came around the 55-minute mark. Striker Tasos Douvikas netted the second, with Paz grabbing the assist (Getty) However, even that dissipated almost as soon as it began. Instead of clawing one back the visitors found themselves three down in the blink of an eye, with Paz nicking the ball off Baleba before driving into the area and steering a finish into the far corner. The third goal summed up the farcical nature of United’s performance, in what was one of their worst displays on the European stage, but there is always time for more embarrassment with this side. Indeed, it came with just under 15 minutes left, with Como centre-back Jacobo Ramon powering in a header when unmarked in the box to give Como a fourth. Joshua Zirkzee scored a late consolation for United, but even that just felt slightly embarrassing. The away end emptied, and as the support from the fans disappeared, you began to think that maybe the hierarchy’s support for Carrick may have too. Paz produced a man of the match display to sink United with two goals and an assist (Reuters) As Lisandro Martinez noted in explosive fashion last week , Carrick has not had the required level of support from the club’s hierarchy. That was clear for all to see on a United bench that contained seven youth team players, with the likes of Martinez, Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu now injured, Leny Yoro suspended and Ayden Heaven out with illness. Everybody knew Martinez was right when he made the comments, though few would have thought it would been illustrated in such emphatic fashion just over a week later. However, there comes a point where the board can’t be blamed for all of the failures on the pitch. The fact remains that Carrick produced some of the leading form in the league with a nearly identical set of players last season, and yet this term he has only managed to produce a series of desperately poor performances, with no sign of an upturn in form on the horizon. It is true that there is little jeopardy for many teams in this new Champions League format, though that does not extend to a United side without a win in seven games. In many ways this was a must-win game for Carrick’s side, especially considering that they’ll have to face Bayern Munich, an in-form Roma side and Sporting away from home among their remaining five league phase games. And yet, rather than winning and potentially stopping the rot for now, they put in one of the worst United performances in living memory. One can complain about support in the form of summer signings, but this was a performance that was created on the training field, not in the boardroom, and the man in the dugout will have to answer for that eventually.

item.title: Utes overcome deficit, force OT, beat Oregon Ducks
item.description: Utah Utes guard TJ Burch (6) and Utah Utes forward Zati Loubaki (80) celebrate after a shot and foul as Utah and Oregon play an exhibition basketball game in the Huntsman Center in Salt Lake City on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News It’s still football season, and it’s possible the Utah men’s basketball team’s first two exhibition contests may have gotten lost in the fans’ conversations about sports up on the hill. But coach Alex Jensen and the players have something they want everyone to know: Playing in the Jon M. Huntsman Center is supposed to mean something. In their third — and final — exhibition game Wednesday night, Trey Campbell and Jackson Holcombe scored 20 points apiece and as the Utes rallied in the final minute to force overtime to overcome the Oregon Ducks 81-77. item.title: Walker Kessler Powers Lakers to Dominant Opening-Night Win Over Warriors
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers, for the second time in the last 10 years, won their opening-night game, taking a 127-105 victory over the Golden State Warriors. The Lakers and Warriors battled closely for a quarter, but Los Angeles’ depth shone through after that. How the Lakers dominated In the first quarter, Steph Curry did what he does best: get his own shot no matter what. He went 7-for-9, with 16 points in that first frame. However, Curry scored seven points in the rest of the game, and the Lakers pulled away, winning the second quarter 32-19 and the third by an even larger margin, 36-16. Oct 21, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) reaches for the ball against Golden State Warriors center Al Horford (20) in the second half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images No surprise, Luka Doncic scored 28 points and totaled seven assists in the first three quarters, going back and forth with Yaxel Lendeborg. Their rivalry peaked right before the first half ended, when he hit a half-court shot over Lendeborg. Luka Doncic belongs in LA, an absolute showstopper. pic.twitter.com/1IlpyCVNQ3 — Nelson Espinal (@nelson__espinal) October 22, 2026 Walker Kessler was the player of the game Halftime, instead of letting the Warriors regroup, kept the ball rolling for the Lakers. They piled it on, and with Curry out of rhythm, the Warriors’ offense had nothing to trouble LA. All night, Walker Kessler dominated in the paint, offering elite rim protection and rim-running, exactly what the Lakers expected from him after the trade and big contract. He finished with 26 points, going 12-for-12 with nine rebounds. All his buckets were dunks, as center Draymond Green had no match for the lob attempts the Lakers were throwing to their big man. Oct 21, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts after scoring against the Golden State Warriors in the first half at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Lakers’ roster-building formula was to add a quality starting big man in Walker Kessler and a boatload of wing players, alongside stars Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic. One game in, that recipe delivered, but tougher tests lie ahead. Who do the Lakers play next? The Lakers play the Clippers on Friday at Crypto.com Arena, a relatively soft test for Doncic and the Lakers as they continue building chemistry. The post Walker Kessler Powers Lakers to Dominant Opening-Night Win Over Warriors appeared first on LA Sports Report .

item.title: Journo thinks what Carrick did immediately after full-time whistle shows he’s on the way out
item.description: Journo thinks what Carrick did immediately after full-time whistle shows he’s on the way out Michael Carrick now finds himself in the same position as every single Manchester United manager post-Sir Alex Ferguson: facing the sack. Last night’s calamitous display away to Champions League newbies Como saw the side round off a seven-game winless streak – their worst since the end of 2015. Carrick appears to be braced for the worst (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) United slumped to a 4-1 defeat in Italy, meaning they have now overseen back-to-back UCL defeats, having lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid last Tuesday. After the referee called time on the visitors’ humiliation and blew his whistle, Carrick went over to the away supporters – those that had stayed until the end – to hold his hands up and apologise. However, Samuel Luckhurst noted that it was a scene akin to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s final outing as United boss, when he did the same after a 4-1 loss to Watford before being relieved of his duties. How did United react? (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Post-match, Carrick did take full responsibility for the torrid performance, though he did remark: “If you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.” Bruno Fernandes, who was surprisingly withdrawn in the 66th minute when United were trailing 3-0, spoke openly on the coaching staff’s chosen tactics, seemingly looking to make it clear to fans that the squad is only doing what they’ve been told to do. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the captain told TNT Sports. Further pressed on whether he believed Carrick got said tactics wrong , Fernandes responded: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: Browns Give Concerning News on Carson Schwesinger
item.description: Carson Schwesinger #49 of the Cleveland Browns Getty As we’ve seen already in a year-plus with Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger in the mix, it takes a lot to keep him off a football field. Schwesinger did not play in the finale of the NFL season in 2025, on orders from the team, as he was fending off the effects of ankle and leg injuries that had built up throughout the season. And we saw him fight through an ankle injury in Week 5 against the Jets in New York, an injury that had him in a walking boot after the game. That same ankle injury made him a gametime decision on Sunday against Baltimore at home, and ultimately, it was decided he could play. He recorded a season-high 13 tackles and forced a critical fumble in that win. So, he has established he can play through whatever he’s got going on with his ankle. The issue is that the ankle injury is still lingering, now 10 days after it originally occurred. We know that because Schwesinger, according to beat reporters in Berea, sat out Browns practice on Wednesday. He’ll probably still play on Sunday, but it’s worrying that the injury is still there. Carson Schwesinger Lobbied to Play After Schwesinger’s big forced fumble on Derrick Henry on Sunday, Browns coach Todd Monken was asked about whether he had an inkling that Schwesinger would play despite sometimes visibly limping. Said Monken: “What’s interesting is early in the week, the trainers were semi-optimistic, but they said, ‘well, it’s Carson.’ And every time I’d see Carson, and I’d ask him, he would get this silly smirk on his face, like, ‘do you know who you’re talking to?’ Like, ‘if I can go, I’m going to go.’ And then we worked him out Friday, and he was going through the bags, and he was like, ‘Well, how do I look?’ Like a little kid. “Of course. What did I say? ‘Oh, you look great. I’ve never seen you better. That ankle looks like, I mean, a million bucks .’ And you could just tell, if he could play, he was going to play. LB Carson Schwesinger also will not practice today because of an ankle injury. https://t.co/AS0OE4s1Go — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 21, 2026 Long Way Till Browns Bye Week And that’s good, Schwesinger’s determination is admirable. No doubt, the Browns don’t win that game against the Ravens if Schwesinger does not play. The same would have been said about the game against the Jets, if the Browns had been able to do anything with the fourth-quarter fumble Schwesinger forced that could have set up a scoring drive, if not for a three-and-out by the Browns offense that became a three-and-fumble over the punter’s head disaster to set yp the Jets’ winning touchdown. But, it’s only Week 6. The Browns have three road games and a home game before their mid-November bye week. Schwesinger will likely keep playing on the ankle between now and then–and the team can only hope it heals anyway. item.title: Linus Ullmark Injury Update: Why Senators Goalie Left Game After Something Simple
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 12: Linus Ullmark #35 of the Ottawa Senators looks on during the second period of a NHL game against the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center on October 12, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Andrew Mordzynski/Getty Images) Getty The Ottawa Senators have gotten off to a hot start to the new season in large part because of their goalie, Linus Ullmark. Everything may have changed for the Sens on Wednesday night, though. Ullmark left their matchup with the Florida Panthers due to injury. It was a big night for Ottawa, which was facing Brady Tkachuk for the first time since trading him away, so emotions were in a hyped-up place for this evening to begin with. But the emotional swing of seeing the star goalie leave the ice was likely not what any Senators fans would’ve been hoping for out of this game. Linus Ullmark Injury Update It wasn’t immediately clear what happened to Ullmark, but it likely was some sort of muscle injury, because it didn’t come after any kind of major contact. Linus Ullmark leaves the game in clear pain, looks like he pulled a muscle. The Senators injury luck continue to be terrible. Especially for Ullmark who’s been spectacular this season. — Alex Adams (@alexadamsBTP_) October 22, 2026 Ullmark has been one of the best goalies in hockey so far this season, so any absence from him is a huge blow to the Senators. What Happened to Linus Ullmark? Ullmark was injured while parrying a shot from distance. He had to slide from his left to his right to knock a shot away with his right pad. The motion seemed to extend his right leg outward, which could put pressure in the hamstring or groin area, depending on what exactly Ullmark did to make that leg motion happen: Sens goalie Linus Ullmark has left the game with an injury. He was helped off the ice with a trainer https://t.co/pwtmD4WGkS — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) October 22, 2026 Linus Ullmark Stats Ullmark entered the night with a 6-1 record. He had won his first six starts of the year. He was operating with a 94.5% save ratio and a 1.33 goals against average. Wednesday night hadn’t started how Ullmark wanted. The departed Brady Tkachuk scored the game’s first goal, an immediate statement against his former team. But then Ullmark and his teammates stepped up, putting up five unanswered goals for a commanding lead. All was going well until Ullmark had to leave the game. Now, Senators fans will cross their fingers that this isn’t too bad an injury. item.content:encoded: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 12: Linus Ullmark #35 of the Ottawa Senators looks on during the second period of a NHL game against the New Jersey Devils at Prudential Center on October 12, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Andrew Mordzynski/Getty Images) Getty The Ottawa Senators have gotten off to a hot start to the new season in large part because of their goalie, Linus Ullmark. Everything may have changed for the Sens on Wednesday night, though. Ullmark left their matchup with the Florida Panthers due to injury. It was a big night for Ottawa, which was facing Brady Tkachuk for the first time since trading him away, so emotions were in a hyped-up place for this evening to begin with. But the emotional swing of seeing the star goalie leave the ice was likely not what any Senators fans would’ve been hoping for out of this game. Linus Ullmark Injury Update It wasn’t immediately clear what happened to Ullmark, but it likely was some sort of muscle injury, because it didn’t come after any kind of major contact. Linus Ullmark leaves the game in clear pain, looks like he pulled a muscle. The Senators injury luck continue to be terrible. Especially for Ullmark who’s been spectacular this season. — Alex Adams (@alexadamsBTP_) October 22, 2026 Ullmark has been one of the best goalies in hockey so far this season, so any absence from him is a huge blow to the Senators. What Happened to Linus Ullmark? Ullmark was injured while parrying a shot from distance. He had to slide from his left to his right to knock a shot away with his right pad. The motion seemed to extend his right leg outward, which could put pressure in the hamstring or groin area, depending on what exactly Ullmark did to make that leg motion happen: Sens goalie Linus Ullmark has left the game with an injury. He was helped off the ice with a trainer https://t.co/pwtmD4WGkS — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) October 22, 2026 Linus Ullmark Stats Ullmark entered the night with a 6-1 record. He had won his first six starts of the year. He was operating with a 94.5% save ratio and a 1.33 goals against average. Wednesday night hadn’t started how Ullmark wanted. The departed Brady Tkachuk scored the game’s first goal, an immediate statement against his former team. But then Ullmark and his teammates stepped up, putting up five unanswered goals for a commanding lead. All was going well until Ullmark had to leave the game. Now, Senators fans will cross their fingers that this isn’t too bad an injury. item.title: Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo reveals where chemistry stands with Bam Adebayo
item.description: Heat’s Giannis Antetokounmpo reveals where chemistry stands with Bam Adebayo originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat will start the 2026-27 NBA season with higher hopes than they've had in a very long time. The Heat, who have done a lot of positive things over the past few decades, are in a great spot to win at a high level this season with Giannis Antetokounmpo now on the roster. Miami hopes Bam Adebayo and Antetokounmpo will be a great duo, though questions remain about how things will look, especially offensively. Defensively, if Antetokounmpo plays at the level everyone expects, giving 100% effort, Miami should have one of the better defensive frontcourts in the NBA. As for learning each other offensively, it still sounds like that's what the two Heat stars are working on. However, Antetokounmpo recently suggested they feel good about where they are, and that it will only improve the more they play. “I love playing with Bam. I just love interacting with him. He has the same personality as my older brother. They were born on the same day. His personality is familiar to me. I love being around him. I love playing with him. I think the more we get to know one another, the better it’s going to be,” Antetokounmpo said , H/T Heavy. The Heat gave up a ton to land Antetokounmpo this offseason, so if that move doesn't work out, it would be a major disappointment. He'll always be a star-level player, barring something drastic changing over the next couple of months. Outside of a potential injury, there's no reason why he won't be one of the best five players in basketball. Adebayo is also a very good player in his own right, so there's very much to be excited about in Miami. item.title: Packers’ $50 Million WR Listed as Unexpected Trade Candidate
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - DECEMBER 07: Jayden Reed #11 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball during the third quarter against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on December 07, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have watched Christian Watson and Matthew Golden emerge as one of the NFL’s most productive receiving duos. Jayden Reed, meanwhile, has been out since Week 2 with a neck injury that ended his season. That combination has led to an unexpected name appearing in the discussion ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Reed, who signed a $50.25 million extension in April, has been listed as Green Bay’s top trade candidate by one national NFL writer, despite a serious injury that complicates the idea of moving him now. Jayden Reed Named Packers Trade Candidate by FOX Sports In an Oct. 21 feature naming one potential trade candidate for every NFL team, FOX Sports’ Henry McKenna chose Reed for the Packers. His argument centered on how Green Bay has used the 26-year-old and how well its offense has performed without him. “Reed’s currently on IR, but he seems like a player who might be better — and more productive — in another offense. He might provide something different from what Matthew Golden and Christian Watson have to offer. But the Packers don’t really make use of Reed’s talents, and they haven’t missed a beat offensively without him,” McKenna wrote. It’s a notable suggestion for a player Green Bay committed to less than six months ago. Reed received a three-year, $50.25 million extension with $20 million guaranteed, keeping him under contract through 2029. He also has a strong track record when healthy. Reed led the Packers with 793 receiving yards as a rookie in 2023, then topped that with 857 yards in 2024. He scored 14 receiving touchdowns across those two seasons. He has also rushed for 310 yards and three touchdowns in his NFL career. His 2025 campaign was limited to seven games because of injuries, and he managed four catches for 24 yards in two appearances this season before suffering the neck injury against the New York Jets on Sept. 20. Jayden Reed Injury Complicates Any Packers Trade The biggest obstacle to McKenna’s suggestion is Reed’s health. Matt LaFleur confirmed Reed needed neck surgery and wouldn’t play again in 2026. LaFleur said at the time that he didn’t believe the injury would end Reed’s career. That makes a trade before November considerably harder to envision. A team acquiring Reed wouldn’t be getting immediate help for a playoff run, and Green Bay would be parting with a receiver it recently paid to keep for the long term. The Packers’ production without him, however, gives McKenna’s argument some context. Watson has 29 catches for 538 yards and six touchdowns through six games, while Golden has 30 receptions for 501 yards and three scores. Jordan Love has thrown for 1,684 yards and 11 touchdowns. Green Bay has also won three straight games, improving to 4-2

With Reed out for the year, the Packers have also been named a possible trade fit for Chargers receiver Quentin Johnston . Skyy Moore’s recent ankle injury has only added to the questions behind Watson and Golden. McKenna’s suggestion stands in contrast to how LaFleur described Reed after his injury. “He brings so much in versatility and how we use him and just all the different roles,” LaFleur said. That was the vision behind the long-term extension Green Bay handed Reed in April. item.title: Bruno Fernandes unhappy with Michael Carrick’s tactics in dismal Man United defeat to Como
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes wasn’t impressed by the tactic of Michael Carrick during his side’s humiliating 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League . United were outrun, outfought and outplayed by their Italian opponents, with Nico Paz in particular running the visitors ragged – notching two goals and an assist for Cesc Fabregas ’s well-drilled side. It was one of United’s worst performances in their long and storied European history and extends their winless run in all competitions to seven matches and ramp up the pressure on Carrick, who may well be on the brink of the sack. Man United skipper Bruno Fernandes wasn’t happy with the tactics employed by the coaching staff (Reuters) Fernandes was largely ineffective once again as the Red Devils failed to gain a foothold before he was substituted off on 67 minutes, a rare move for the ever-present skipper, and his replacement Joshua Zirkzee scored an injury-time consolation. Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Fernandes criticised United’s tactics, specifically their lack of pressing which gave Como too much time and left them somewhat toothless. “It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” said Fernandes. "I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure." Captain Bruno Fernandes gives his immediate reaction to Manchester United's heavy 4-1 defeat to Como 🗣️ 🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/8bzmLGkRAX — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 When asked whether he was saying that Carrick got his tactics wrong, the Portuguese added: “That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. “As you saw with them [Como], the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to. “A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.” Fernandes was dejected after another defeat for Man United (Reuters) Midfielder Youri Tielemans admitted the performance wasn’t up to scratch, saying: “It was a very bad match from us. The fans come out here and we put out a non-performance like this, it's not good enough from us.” The pressure is mounting on Carrick, with Sunday’s home match against Bournemouth now taking on even more importance. And former United striker Dimitar Berbatov , speaking on TNT after the game, didn’t pull any punches when discussing the Red Devils’ display. item.title: Blue Jays should be one of many suitors for two Chicago Cubs sluggers this winter in MLB free agency
item.description: Blue Jays should be one of many suitors for two Chicago Cubs sluggers this winter in MLB free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays seemingly have more needs than anybody would have imagined entering the offseason a year ago. After making the World Series in 2025, the Blue Jays find themselves in a position nobody expected, and the front office will be tasked with changing that this winter. The expected lockout will create challenges, but the Blue Jays still have a chance to improve offensively, whether it takes a couple of months because of the lockout or they try to get deals done before it. Available players include Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ, both of whom spent the past few seasons with the Chicago Cubs . Happ and Suzuki are both above-average players and would be great additions to a Blue Jays offense that can use all the help it can get. Bleacher Report recently noted that Toronto clearly needs a designated hitter and outfield help. “With Addison Barger coming off a season where he played just nine games and George Springer headed for free agency and perhaps retirement, a corner outfielder and a designated hitter will both be on the offseason shopping list,” Joel Reuter wrote . The Blue Jays have found some success in free agency over the past few years, adding players at high prices. The ownership and front office have shown that they're willing to spend, which is 90% of the battle more often than not. The interesting part, however, is that the Blue Jays will have competition for both of these guys because of the lack of talent in the free-agent class. That could cause Suzuki and Happ to make more money than Toronto is willing to pay. item.title: Darius Garland leads Clippers to big win over Kings
item.description: Clippers guard Darius Garland lets out a yell after scoring against the Kings during the second quarter Wednesday at Intuit Dome. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Darius Garland, microphone in hand, waited patiently at midcourt to speak before the Clippers tipped off their 2026-27 NBA season against the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday night at Intuit Dome. “Clipper Nation, Clipper Nation,” the eighth-year guard said to raucous cheers in Inglewood. “We’ve been working hard all summer, ready to really turn up this year. [We’ll] try to play at the highest level. [I] really appreciate the support from my teammates, coaching staff [and] organization — really appreciate everybody that comes out and … continues to support. We’re gonna be here all year. “Clipper Nation, let’s go.” Garland wasted no time giving Clippers fans something to smile about after an offseason of torment and transformation. He started the game shooting five-for-five from the field and three-for-three from deep, scoring 16 points in nine minutes and fueling the Clippers’ 121-96 blowout win over the Kings . item.content:encoded: Clippers guard Darius Garland lets out a yell after scoring against the Kings during the second quarter Wednesday at Intuit Dome. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Darius Garland, microphone in hand, waited patiently at midcourt to speak before the Clippers tipped off their 2026-27 NBA season against the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday night at Intuit Dome. “Clipper Nation, Clipper Nation,” the eighth-year guard said to raucous cheers in Inglewood. “We’ve been working hard all summer, ready to really turn up this year. [We’ll] try to play at the highest level. [I] really appreciate the support from my teammates, coaching staff [and] organization — really appreciate everybody that comes out and … continues to support. We’re gonna be here all year. “Clipper Nation, let’s go.” Garland wasted no time giving Clippers fans something to smile about after an offseason of torment and transformation. He started the game shooting five-for-five from the field and three-for-three from deep, scoring 16 points in nine minutes and fueling the Clippers’ 121-96 blowout win over the Kings . Darius Garland scores the first three points of the #Clippers ’ season👌 pic.twitter.com/G9h16vMNNn — Joaquin Ruiz (@WalkingRuiz) October 22, 2026 Beginning his first full season in Los Angeles after being acquired from Cleveland in a trade for James Harden in February, Garland led the Clippers with 30 points on 11-for-19 shooting and four assists. Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis, meanwhile, did the heavy lifting for Sacramento, with the shooting guard scoring 28 points and the center facilitating the offense with 14 points, eight assists and 18 rebounds. Key Kings forward Keegan Murray was scoreless through the first three quarters and was held to just two points. And rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr., whom Sacramento selected No. 7 in the draft out of Arkansas, posted 12 points on an abysmal five-for-24 shooting in his debut. The Clippers, however, had fun to start the post-Kawhi Leonard era. Following Garland’s lead, L.A.’s returners, including forward Derrick Jones Jr., guard Kris Dunn and centers Isaiah Jackson and Brook Lopez, were efficient and productive. Jones finished with eight points, five assists, six rebounds and an electric alley-oop slam; Dunn had seven points, seven assists and five rebounds with his usual hard-nosed defense; Jackson had 13 points and five rebounds; and Lopez had 17 points and 11 rebounds. But Clippers fans were plenty focused on the new guys. Former Lakers forward Rui Hachimura, who signed a three-year deal with the crosstown rival in the offseason, struggled in his Clippers debut and finished with 10 points on three-for-13 shooting. Guard Gradey Dick, a piece of the offseason trade that sent Leonard back to Toronto, was far more productive with 12 points. Then there’s the rookie out of Illinois. Keaton Wagler, the Clippers’ No. 5 pick in the draft, posted 15 points with five assists and five rebounds off the bench. The team’s highest draft pick since Blake Griffin (No. 1 in 2009) was clearly comfortable from the jump and gave his new fan base plenty to be hopeful for. “He’s already shown that he’s mature,” coach Tyronn Lue said pregame. “I think he doesn’t get rattled, and just being around him for the last few months, whether he’s making shots [or] missing shots [and] not playing well, he’s always the same. He has the confidence to just keep shooting the balls, even when he’s missing.” Wagler had an assist on his first touch and converted a savvy layup for his first career points. Clippers rookie G Keaton Wagler scores the first points of his NBA career 🫰 pic.twitter.com/XNulM76WM7 — Joaquin Ruiz (@WalkingRuiz) October 22, 2026 Fellow rookie Baba Miller, a forward the Clippers drafted with the No. 36 pick, finished with four points and three rebounds. Lue — whose first starting lineup featured Garland, Dunn, Jones Jr., Hachimura and Jackson — and the Clippers are in unfamiliar territory without a superstar on the roster and with most outsiders expecting the team’s streak of 15 consecutive plus-.500 campaigns to end. But as Clippers interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden nervously said on media day, the team works well with its back against the wall. Injury updates The Clippers said guard Bradley Beal (knee), center Yanic Konan Niederhauser (foot) and forwards Brandon Ingram (heel) and Max Strus (foot) are all making progress in their rehab journeys but won’t travel for the team’s first road game on Sunday against the Oklahoma City Thunder. item.title: Mets should pursue one of two Chicago Cubs stars, even with Juan Soto and Carson Benge
item.description: Mets should pursue one of two Chicago Cubs stars, even with Juan Soto and Carson Benge originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Given how average the New York Mets were offensively a season ago, it feels safe to say something has to give regarding adding a player or two this offseason. The Mets seem set in the outfield right now, led by Juan Soto, A.J. Ewing, and Carson Benge, but they could also decide to ignore certain positions and focus on fielding the best possible lineup. In that scenario, targeting a couple of offensive players this offseason could be a wise move. Two guys in particular who fit that bill are Seiya Suzuki and Ian Happ. Bleacher Report recently suggested both could interest the Mets, even with the existing outfield looking set. “The Mets appear to have their present and future outfield in place with Juan Soto and 2026 rookies Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing, but designated hitter is a potential area to upgrade. The DH spot produced a .213/.310/.378 line this past season, and with their limitless budget, a run at signing Suzuki to fill that hole is not out of the question,” Joel Reuter wrote . Soto is one of the best players in baseball, Benge has a real chance to be a superstar, and Ewing looks like a guy the Mets can count on for a long time. All three of those guys will be in the lineup every day, or should be, but that doesn't mean bringing in a guy like Suzuki or Happ has to change that. The only question for the Mets is whether they're willing to spend money on those guys, since they could be expensive given the lack of talent. item.title: What Did Angry Troy Aikman Tell Joe Buck in Heated MNF Spat? Report Has Answer
item.description: What did Troy Aikman say to Joe Buck during their heated Monday Night Football confrontation? A new report sheds light on the ESPN broadcasters' dispute. Getty Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have shared an NFL broadcast booth for 25 seasons, but a heated pregame argument at SoFi Stadium has exposed a rift over Buck’s new ESPN contract. Aikman felt blindsided by a deal he never knew existed, according to multiple reports. The two now face the remainder of the NFL season plus the Super Bowl in the same booth. The new details come from more than a dozen sources, according to Puck reporter Dylan Byers. The argument erupted before the Oct. 12 game in which the Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 in overtime. Aikman had spent weeks growing “increasingly cold, difficult, short,” one source told Byers, as quoted by Pro Football Talk‘s Mike Florio. Buck “finally snapped,” according to the new report. “He basically said, ‘Dude, are we really going to do this?’ And Troy’s position was: You f***** me over!” the source told Byers. Read More From Heavy Troy Aikman Rips Bears’ Ben Johnson Decision Before Chicago Routs Eagles Troy Aikman’s Contract Dispute With Joe Buck So what set Aikman off? A six-year extension that keeps Buck as the voice of Monday Night Football through ESPN’s next Super Bowl, a deal that became public Sept. 16, according to The Athletic . Buck negotiated it in May, and neither he, ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro nor their shared agency, CAA, told Aikman, according to the Byers report. Aikman “saw it as the ultimate act of betrayal,” a source told Byers. “They cut this deal in May and put it in a drawer,” the source added. “ESPN didn’t tell him, Joe didn’t tell him.” Aikman is in the final year of a five-year contract worth about $90 million (roughly $18 million annually) and has no formal offer from ESPN or parent company Disney. One of his agents set his value near $30 million a year and talks stalled, according to Sports Media Watch . The friction surfaced Oct. 14. Buck “broke the ice” before kickoff, and the argument that followed de-escalated, according to Front Office Sports . Aikman did not deny the tension on Dallas radio station 96.7 The Ticket. “I’ll broadcast through this season and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens,” Aikman said, as quoted by Sports Media Watch . Buck apologized to Aikman and the production crew before the following Monday’s Commanders – 49ers game. “We’re all adults, we’ve all got jobs to do, let’s move forward, let’s have a great year,” Buck said, per Byers’ reporting. Aikman reportedly said nothing. item.title: Los Angeles Rams Deliver Bad News About $22 Million Starter
item.description: The Rams provided an unfortunate update on Nate Landman to open Week 7. Getty The Los Angeles Rams must prepare to be without linebacker Nate Landman in Week 7. Landman was among the multitude of players Rams head coach Sean McVay provided status updates on to begin the week of preparation before facing the Las Vegas Raiders. McVay also provided information on cornerbacks Josh Wallace and Trent McDuffie–a two-time Super Bowl champion and one of LA’s big 2026 offseason trade acquisitions–and tight end Colby Parkinson. “For today, Trent will be a DNP with his groin [injury]. We’ll take it a day at a time, kind of like what I told you guys, and kind of evaluate his status as we go. And then on Monday, kind of found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol,” McVay told reporters on October 21. “He’ll be on a DNP. “And then, Josh Wallace and Colby Parkinson will both be full.” Landman is a two-time team captain in his second season with the Rams. He had a breakout season in 2025 and is on track to record a career-high in tackles this season. A find for the Rams in free agency from the Atlanta Falcons in 2025, Landman is signed through 2028 on a three-year, $22.5 million contract . The Rams could go in a few different directions if Landman is unable to clear the five-step concussion protocol in time for game day in Week 7. Rams Eyeing All-Pro to Replace Nate Landman Landman, who turns 28 in November, appeared in every game for the Rams in 2025, regular and postseason. His playmaking ability proved just as valuable as his ability to make a stop reliably for the Rams defense. The Rams already have a replacement option in mind if Landman cannot play in Week 7. That is one-time Pro Bowler and First Team All-Pro Eric Kendricks, which McVay confirmed during his presser. “It could be a possibility,” McVay said. “He’s done a great job. And you can see, just being around him, a guy that’s played a lot of good, quality football. I have tremendous respect for him just coaching against him when he’s been at his different stops. And then, obviously, he’s really done a nice job in the couple weeks that he’s been here. So, he is certainly a candidate if that was necessary.” Kendricks, 34, has a longer track record than Landman, posting at least 108 total tackles for nine straight seasons, most recently in 2024. Kendricks would join Omar Speights in the starting lineup, but the Rams have other options. Second-year pro Shaun Dolac and special teams ace Grant Stuard are on the 53-man roster. The Rams also have Elias Neal, another second-year former UDFA, on the practice squad with Kendricks. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Los Angeles Rams Deliver Bad News About $22 Million Starter appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Why Isn’t Brandon Ingram Playing Tonight? When Clippers Star Might Return After Trade
item.description: Brandon Ingram now of the Clippers Getty Through no fault of Brandon Ingram, he had to wait. The Los Angeles Clippers traded away Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors this offseason, and Ingram was one of the pieces that came back to L.A. Except the deal didn’t go through right away. The off-court saga involving Leonard and impermissible payments dragged on, and it meant no one was quite sure whether the trade would actually be approved by the league in the end. It created the odd possibility that Ingram might have to return to the team that traded him away. In the end, though, Ingram was good to go — the Clippers brought him aboard, Leonard went to Toronto and both sides will now move forward. Well, sort of. The Clippers aren’t really moving anywhere with Ingram at the moment. The Clippers begin their season on Wednesday night against the Sacramento Kings . All that Ingram will be doing is watching. Why Isn’t Brandon Ingram Playing Tonight? Ingram isn’t playing on Wednesday night as the Clippers open their season because he’s injured. The forward underwent surgery on his right heel in May. It’s the recovery from that which is keeping Ingram out of action. When is Brandon Ingram Coming Back? There isn’t yet an official timetable on Ingram’s return. Heel injuries and surgeries aren’t as common as some others, and so there isn’t as much precedent to go on. In the NFL, Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce had surgery on his heel in the offseason, made it back in time for Week 1, but then re-injured the same heel in Week 2 and had to go on injured reserve. While it’s far from the same sport, and it’s hard to know how similar the injuries are, it is a recent example of the heel recovery not being straightforward, either. Other Clippers Injuries The worst part of the Clippers missing Ingram due to injury is that he’s not the only guy who is out. Bradley Beal is missing opening night due to right knee injury management. Jordan Miller is out because he had surgery on his left rotator cuff. Yanic Konan Niederhauser is sitting out after right lisfranc surgery. And new acquisition Max Strus has a partial tear of his right plantar fascia and is being held out of the opener. The likes of Darius Garland and Keaton Wagler are gonna have a ton of work to do on the perimeter to get the ball in the basket. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Why Isn’t Brandon Ingram Playing Tonight? When Clippers Star Might Return After Trade appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Bills suddenly considered suitor for $20M DB the Titans recently benched
item.description: Bills suddenly considered suitor for $20M DB the Titans recently benched originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills have to feel good about what they've done on both sides of the ball to start this season, though there are still ways for this team to improve. Buffalo, currently in first place in the AFC East with a 5-1 record, is coming off two impressive wins against the Los Angeles Rams and Las Vegas Raiders . However, over the past three games, the Bills have given up at least 29 points in each. That's not a recipe for success come playoff time, and the front office will have to figure it out. Among the Bills' needs on both sides of the ball, adding help in the secondary is at the top of the list. According to the latest report, they could link up with the Tennessee Titans in a trade for Alontae Taylor, a guy who has struggled a bit this season in Tennessee and isn't playing as much as some would expect after being a healthy scratch in Week 6. “Bills – Titans CB Alontae Taylor: The Titans love them some drama and deciding to bench their best corner, who they just signed to a $20M/year deal, six weeks into his tenure there, is right on brand. Buffalo desperately needs to address serious issues on the back end; they don’t have really three NFL quality boundary corners, and Taylor was very good with the Saints . Weird time to rework a brand new free-agent deal for a trade, but Buffalo GM Brandon Beane is quite good, and there are not many corners who could get dealt,” Jason La Canfora wrote . Taylor certainly isn't a perfect player, and that's been evident throughout some of this season. However, as Buffalo looks to win a Super Bowl, bringing in a veteran like him who can make a difference would be a wise move. For now, it's unclear what the Titans would want for the 27-year-old, but after sitting him, it seems safe to say he could be available.
