item.title: Bam Adebayo reveals the Heat were overthinking the first game of the season
item.description: Bam Adebayo reveals the Heat were overthinking the first game of the season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Miami Heat did not have the best season opener as they lost to the Minnesota Timberwolves in a blowout. It was a disappointing defeat for the new-look Heat with Giannis Antetokounmpo. It seemed the Heat got too eager because the Timberwolves dominated them. Antetokounmpo tried his best with a 35-point performance, but the rest of the team struggled. This led to Bam Adebayo looking back on what happened, and he gave the reason behind the loss. Bam Adebayo provides the context behind the Heat's first loss As the leader and captain for the Heat, Adebayo was realistic with his reaction after the game. He even joked about how head coach Erik Spoelstra will make them watch back their defensive performance. Giving up 131 points to the Timberwolves on opening night is not a good look for the Heat. However, they will have to learn from it because they have to meet the sky-high expectations. MORE: Giannis Antetokounmpo breaks a LeBron James record in his debut for the Heat Antetokounmpo lived up to the hype with his performance, but it seems that the rest of the Heat might have been too eager. At least, that is what Adebayo believes happened during the season opener at home. "I think that build-up of wanting to play so good in front of our home crowd and obviously set the tone was not there. We’re gonna get back to the drawing board, watch film, now it’s real," Adebayo said about what happened to the Heat's loss on opening night . This is an eye-opening loss for the Heat, as they will have to meet expectations. It will be challenging, but they are seemingly ready to do so moving forward, especially with Adebayo already addressing the problem. item.title: Former Vikings QB J.J. McCarthy Gets Candid Ahead of Giants Start
item.description: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) Getty It’s been a couple of weeks since the Minnesota Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick. Nonetheless, McCarthy now has an opportunity for a fresh start, as the Giants named him the starting QB on Oct. 21 for their Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. The Giants‘ decision to turn to the former Vikings starter stems from his Week 6 performance against the New Orleans Saints ; McCarthy entered in the fourth quarter with New York trailing 34-10, replacing Jameis Winston. He sparked a late rally that brought the Giants within reach of a comeback victory. McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception, finishing with a 90.0 passer rating. Although the Giants fell short, it appears as though it was enough to warrant a start. Ahead of his Week 7 start with the Giants, McCarthy discussed what he learned during his time with the Vikings and why he feels better prepared for his next opportunity as a starting quarterback. “I believe just experience does wonders,” McCarthy told reporters on Oct. 21 . “Being able to be in that same situation where you might have made a mistake the last time, this time you’re just going to react better and make a more well-rounded response decision in that situation. “Just being around great talent and great coaches, absolutely love everyone on the offensive side of the ball and the defensive side of the ball does a tremendous job of just giving us opportunities and always making sure we stay in the game and fight till the last seconds of each game.” Vikings’ Brian O’Neill on J.J. McCarthy’s Week 6 Performance With McCarthy off on the right foot in New York, Vikings offensive tackle Brian O’Neill shared his candid thoughts on seeing his former teammate find success. “I didn’t watch it live, but I was getting some texts while it was going on, and then I saw the highlights after,” O’Neill said during an Oct. 21 appearance on KFAN . “I was really happy for him. I think you saw how happy the New York Giants sideline was for him. That’s cool. “You want guys to be able to have a chance to play, and I’m happy he’s stepped in and played well. Who knows what’ll happen the rest of the year, but he’s going to be ready if they call his number.” Giants’ John Harbaugh on J.J. McCarthy’s Tenure S0 Far Moreover, Giants head coach John Harbaugh shared his thoughts on the decision to go with McCarthy, noting that the players know who the good players are on the team and know who gives them the best chance to win which might explain the QB switch as the NFC East is wide open for anyone to win. “I’d watched him a lot in college, but now I need to watch tape, and then I’m watching the tape, and you see good, and you see the not good and all that,” Harbaugh told reporters on Oct. 21 . “But I saw a lot of talent, and I saw a guy that I thought could do the things that we want to do on offense for sure. item.title: Cowboys get trade rumor on Maxx Crosby and another star edge rusher
item.description: Cowboys get trade rumor on Maxx Crosby and another star edge rusher originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jerry Jones made it clear on Wednesday that if his team has a chance to make a move to improve at the trade deadline, he's willing to do it. For now, it's unclear what the Cowboys are looking for at this year's deadline, but the most obvious move would be to land an edge rusher. The Cowboys' inability to get stops at a high level has been evident through the first couple of weeks of the season, and adding more pressure on the quarterback could help fix that. Per the latest report, Dallas could be interested in two candidates. Both names would be excellent additions in Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals and Maxx Crosby of the Las Vegas Raiders . “Cowboys – Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat/Raiders EDGE Maxx Crosby: The Cowboys defense needs help for years to come. Owner Jerry Jones needs more than a rental for a few games to try to get into the playoffs. They need dudes they can hopefully build around. “Arizona is in full tank mode and will likely make at least three more trades (Sweat, RB James Conner once he is healthy, and a QB)... Jones has a close relationship with both ownership groups and could probably go over the heads of some of their football people to try to get what he wants,” Jason La Canfora wrote . There seems to be more expectation that Sweat will be available, as the Cardinals have struggled over the past couple of weeks. Las Vegas is also a questionable team in the sense that it likely isn't a contender, and it already tried to trade Crosby but failed after the Baltimore Ravens backed out of the deal this past offseason. Crosby would be a better addition, but Sweat is also a very good player and could help this team. item.title: 'It was an historic night' - Two-goal hero Nico Paz praises team-mates after Como inflict humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat on Manchester United
item.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-COMO-MAN UNITED - AFP Como playmaker Nico Paz has hailed his team-mates after scoring twice and providing an assist in Wednesday's stunning 4-1 Champions League rout of Manchester United. The Argentine star inspired Cesc Fabregas' fearless side to a famous victory at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia that heaps pressure on visiting boss Michael Carrick. Midfielder orchestrates stunning victory Paz expressed deep appreciation for his colleagues following a watershed evening that stunned European football . Having previously swept aside RB Leipzig, the Serie A upstarts achieved the unprecedented feat of netting four goals across their opening pair of home fixtures in a maiden continental campaign. Furthermore, this emphatic outcome places them alongside AC Milan as the only domestic outfits to crush the English giants by a three-goal deficit in European history. Playmaker terrorises visiting defence imago-sport-1084868783.jpg Diogo Dalot spurned an early chance before Paz struck inside two minutes, collecting possession near the penalty arc, shifting onto his left boot, and curling beyond Senne Lammens. At 22 years and 43 days old, the South American sensation became the second-youngest player from his continent to score against United in the tournament, trailing only Lionel Messi's landmark effort in the 2009 final . The influential schemer maintained complete authority after the break, sliding a precise pass for Tasos Douvikas to extend the advantage before intercepting a loose clearance to notch his second. Delighted with his individual display, the Man of the Match told TNT Sports : "It's one of the most special nights of my life and my career, for me and for the club. It was an historic night because we played against one of the best clubs ever and to do this at home is incredible. We're very happy with our performance." Highlighting the collective backing from the bench and dressing room, the young talisman continued: "I felt so good out there. I enjoyed this game very much. I am surrounded by amazing team-mates and that allows me to play my game. I'm very happy to play in this team, also because of the staff that give me lots of confidence." Debutants savour elite adventure Como goalkeeper Jean Butez turned away Amad Diallo's effort prior to Kaiki Bruno providing an unhindered cross for Jacobo Ramon to head home number four, while Lammens denied Paz a late hat-trick. Joshua Zirkzee grabbed a stoppage-time consolation for the travelling contingent after replacing Bruno Fernandes midway through the second period. Emphasising the importance of maintaining momentum following their remarkable rise from amateur tiers, Paz added: "We have to enjoy every game like we did today. We have to try to repeat this performance. This is historic, it's the first time we are in the Champions League, and we have to enjoy it." item.title: Chiefs suddenly viewed as landing spot for WR not named Tyreek Hill
item.description: Chiefs suddenly viewed as landing spot for WR not named Tyreek Hill originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Reports over the past couple of months indicate the Kansas City Chiefs could be interested in bringing back Tyreek Hill. For now, Hill's future in the NFL remains uncertain due to off-the-field issues. In other areas, adding another wide receiver besides Hill seems to be at the top of the priority list. The Chiefs have been the best team in football to start this season, perhaps outside of the San Francisco 49ers , and look to have a legitimate chance to win a Super Bowl. However, they still need a wide receiver, which is why the latest suggestion that Kansas City could be interested in veteran Chris Godwin makes a ton of sense. “Chiefs – Buccaneers WR Chris Godwin: How much of his decline is due to the fact the Bucs haven’t been able to push the ball downfield for years and Baker Mayfield was not good or healthy least year and same thing this year? And the loss of Mike Evans has set Tampa’s pass game back? “The Chiefs likely need more than one roll of the dice at the receiver position given all their issues there, and lack of another playmaker was a concern even before the season began. "Even if they sign (free agent WR Tyreek) Hill, Andy (Reid) is going to want to do something else," said an NFL exec who knows Reid well and used to work with him,” Jason La Canfora wrote . Godwin has been a very good player for much of his career, but he's dealt with injuries as well. He's been decent this year for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but hasn't been the same type of player that we're used to seeing. Much of that could be because Baker Mayfield is injured, though it's also fair to wonder if the 30-year-old is slowing down a bit. On the season, Godwin has 23 receptions for 260 yards, averaging 9.4 yards per catch. He hasn't scored a touchdown yet. item.title: ‘Humiliating’ – NFL’s Cincinnati Bengals’ treatment of Vice President JD Vance draws fan attention
item.description: Photo by Jacquelyn Martin-Pool/Getty Images U.S. Vice President JD Vance went inside the Cincinnati Bengals locker room after their practice on October 21 to greet the players, but it didn’t go to plan. President Donald Trump has found ways to ingratiate himself with many people in the sports world, bringing out multiple NFL players and legends to publicly support and endorse him for the job he is doing as the country’s President. Vice President Vance tried to interact with an NFL team after their latest practice session and found the reception much colder than what the President has received around athletes over the last two years. JD Vance’s cold interaction with the Bengals has fans talking Vice President Vance stood in the locker room as the Bengals players finished practice, with nobody except TE Drew Sample shaking Vance’s hand, with the other players seemingly ignoring Vance’s presence. Another video did show Vance interacting with star WR Ja’Marr Chase, but outside of that, it seemed to be a very cold reception, something that fans did not ignore on social media. “One guy on the entire team acknowledges the existence of the vice president of the United States who is standing just feet away. Humiliating,” said one fan, labelling this as a humiliating experience for the VP . “I’ve never seen a group of people less enthusiastic to meet the vice president. They barely looked his way,” said another fan . “Looks like he got ignored by 95% of the roster lol,” was the main takeaway for one fan . “interesting that most of them ignored him,” observed a fan . “Good for the Bengal players. Vance is an obnoxious jerk,” were the thoughts of another fan . The Bengals were likely exhausted after an intensive training session before a high-stakes clash against the 4-2 Baltimore Ravens. Vance is an Ohio native and likely roots for the Bengals, so he will probably feel negatively about this interaction. At least he did get visible support from TE Sample and spoke to Chase in the hallway; otherwise, this would have looked a lot worse for the popular support the VP carries. item.title: Luka Doncic Leads Lakers to Dominant Season Opening Win Over Warriors
item.description: Photo by: Kirby Lee The Los Angeles Lakers opened the 2026-27 NBA season in impressive fashion Wednesday night, defeating the Golden State Warriors 127-105 at Crypto.com Arena. Luka Doncic led the way with 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists, while new center Walker Kessler delivered a spectacular debut as Los Angeles dominated the second and third quarters. The victory gave the Lakers an encouraging start to a new era following LeBron James’ departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. With Doncic now firmly established as the team’s centerpiece, Los Angeles showed plenty of offensive firepower against a familiar Western Conference rival. Doncic and Kessler Power the Lakers Doncic controlled the game with his scoring and playmaking, repeatedly creating opportunities for himself and his teammates. His biggest highlight came at the end of the first half, when he connected on a half-court buzzer-beater to give Los Angeles a 66-52 lead. Kessler was equally impressive in his Lakers debut. The big man scored 26 points, grabbed nine rebounds and made all 12 of his field goal attempts. His finishing around the rim gave Golden State major problems and provided Doncic with a reliable option inside. Austin Reaves added 23 points and six assists, continuing his role as one of the Lakers’ most important offensive players. Quentin Grimes and Jake LaRavia each contributed 10 points as Los Angeles received production throughout its rotation. Lakers Take Control After Halftime Golden State initially looked competitive, with Stephen Curry scoring 16 points in the opening quarter. Curry finished with 23 points, but the Warriors struggled to maintain their early momentum. Los Angeles outscored Golden State 32-19 in the second quarter before delivering an even more decisive third-quarter performance. The Lakers won the period 36-16, extending their advantage to 102-68 entering the final quarter. The Lakers’ efficient shooting and ability to capitalize on turnovers helped create a lead the Warriors could not overcome. Golden State struggled defensively, particularly when trying to contain Kessler around the basket. A Strong Start to the New Era The Lakers finished with a convincing 22-point victory, offering an early glimpse of their potential with Doncic leading the offense and Kessler strengthening the interior. Golden State will need to improve defensively and find more consistent support for Curry as the season progresses. For Los Angeles, the opening night performance was exactly what the team needed. The Lakers have plenty of adjustments ahead, but their dominant win provides an encouraging foundation for the season.
item.content:encoded: Photo by: Kirby Lee The Los Angeles Lakers opened the 2026-27 NBA season in impressive fashion Wednesday night, defeating the Golden State Warriors 127-105 at Crypto.com Arena. Luka Doncic led the way with 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists, while new center Walker Kessler delivered a spectacular debut as Los Angeles dominated the second and third quarters. The victory gave the Lakers an encouraging start to a new era following LeBron James’ departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. With Doncic now firmly established as the team’s centerpiece, Los Angeles showed plenty of offensive firepower against a familiar Western Conference rival. Doncic and Kessler Power the Lakers Doncic controlled the game with his scoring and playmaking, repeatedly creating opportunities for himself and his teammates. His biggest highlight came at the end of the first half, when he connected on a half-court buzzer-beater to give Los Angeles a 66-52 lead. Kessler was equally impressive in his Lakers debut. The big man scored 26 points, grabbed nine rebounds and made all 12 of his field goal attempts. His finishing around the rim gave Golden State major problems and provided Doncic with a reliable option inside. Austin Reaves added 23 points and six assists, continuing his role as one of the Lakers’ most important offensive players. Quentin Grimes and Jake LaRavia each contributed 10 points as Los Angeles received production throughout its rotation. Lakers Take Control After Halftime Golden State initially looked competitive, with Stephen Curry scoring 16 points in the opening quarter. Curry finished with 23 points, but the Warriors struggled to maintain their early momentum. Los Angeles outscored Golden State 32-19 in the second quarter before delivering an even more decisive third-quarter performance. The Lakers won the period 36-16, extending their advantage to 102-68 entering the final quarter. The Lakers’ efficient shooting and ability to capitalize on turnovers helped create a lead the Warriors could not overcome. Golden State struggled defensively, particularly when trying to contain Kessler around the basket. A Strong Start to the New Era The Lakers finished with a convincing 22-point victory, offering an early glimpse of their potential with Doncic leading the offense and Kessler strengthening the interior. Golden State will need to improve defensively and find more consistent support for Curry as the season progresses. For Los Angeles, the opening night performance was exactly what the team needed. The Lakers have plenty of adjustments ahead, but their dominant win provides an encouraging foundation for the season.

item.title: Angel Reese gives props to Dream crowd for showing up in Game 3 vs. Valkyries
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Angel Reese gives props to Dream crowd for showing up in Game 3 vs. Valkyries appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After their win in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals , Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese issued a simple request before the best-of-seven series shifted to State Farm Arena. Reese urged their home crowd to “pull up” and “pop up.” Her alliterative plea did not fall on deaf ears, as 17,000 fans trooped to Game 3. The Dream fulfilled their end of the bargain , beating the Valkyries, 97-71, to inch closer to winning their first-ever title. As she has done all season, the 26-year-old Reese gave credit to their home crowd for their unflinching support . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I thought Ballhalla was loud, but Atlanta, y’all came out, and on a Wednesday, on a school night, you got work tomorrow. I appreciate y’all for coming out and supporting us and being loud on every single possession, just cheering,” said Reese in the video posted by WSB-TV’s Alison Mastrangelo. “Now, you don’t have work on Sunday. You got church, maybe. But Saturday, you better pull up. Run it back, run it back. I’m looking forward to it.” Angel Reese extremely impressed with the Atlanta crowd tonight. Mentions I know you all might have church on Sunday, but you all better be out there on Saturday afternoon. #WNBAfinals #Finals pic.twitter.com/EkQ7Np55KR — Alison Mastrangelo (@AlisonWSB) October 22, 2026 Reese finished with a double-double of 21 points and 12 rebounds, both team-highs, on top of three assists and three steals. Rhyne Howard added 16 points, four rebounds, four assists, and five steals, while Jordin Canada tallied 10 points, six rebounds, and eight assists. Just a few days before the WNBA Finals, the Dream faced a scheduling conflict that threatened to force them to play at Gateway Center Arena, which holds only 3,500 fans. The WNBA, however, found a solution, allowing the Dream to play at State Farm Arena. Related: Dream star Angel Reese enters ultra-rare A’ja Wilson WNBA Finals club with absurd streak Related: Karl Smesko sends powerful message as Dream go up 2-1 over Valkyries

item.title: Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves spoil Giannis' home debut with Heat
item.description: As far as debuts go, in this one with the Miami Heat , Giannis Antetokounmpo was exceptional . He set the record for most points during a debut in franchise history with 35 – a mark previously held by LeBron James. He set the tone with a 21-point first half on a barrage of downhill drives and finishes at the rim, giving the Heat a legitimate Most Valuable Player candidate they haven’t had since James was on the roster. He played with pace and was practically impossible to guard in transition and in the paint, where he scored a game-high 24 points. Yet – and it’s essential to point out here that it’s merely one game and that it was always going to take some time for this group to find its potential – the Heat will be in trouble if they cannot do these two things. Miami bricked 3-pointer after 3-pointer on Wednesday, Oct. 21 in the 131-106 beating it caught in their much-anticipated season opener, which is concerning because this was precisely the weak spot the team was facing headed into the season. The Heat also got torched on defense, especially along the perimeter, which fed into the offensive struggles. Miami traded away much of its young core and had to scramble during the offseason to add worthy shooters. And on a team with Antetokounmpo as its centerpiece, shooting is a non-negotiable. Antetokounmpo carries so much gravity when he has the ball in his hands, sucking defenders into the paint, which tends to leave players wide open in the perimeter. It’s why Antetokounmpo has averaged at least 5.4 assists per game each of the last 10 seasons. Yet, Miami made only 8-of-33 attempts (24.2%) from 3-point range. Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Nikola Jović, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Pelle Larsson – players expected to convert catch-and-shoot looks – combined to go 3-of-20 (15%). “We didn’t get many good looks,” Heat coach Erik Spoelstra told reporters after the game. “(Antetokounmpo) was a force of nature, for sure, doing what he does. But we didn’t look like us offensively.” In fact, it was so bad for the Heat that Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who dropped 45 on Miami, actually made one more 3-pointer (nine total) than the entire Heat lineup. Spoelstra went on to say that Miami did “uncharacteristic” things, but he was generous with the good looks comment. A lot of them were with plenty of space. The issue was that role players seemingly still don’t know how to play with Antetokounmpo, with many resorting to standing around, waiting for the ball to come to them. Compounding the poor shooting was relative disinterest on defense. This is particularly uncharacteristic of Spoelstra and the Heat, who pride themselves on making everything difficult for opponents. Minnesota shot 46.9% from the field, which is fine – Miami was actually more efficient at 48.1% – but the Timberwolves unloaded from deep, draining 21-of-50 attempts (42%). The edge of converted 3-pointers for the Timberwolves, 13, created a differential of 39 points. Very few teams, if

He set the record for most points during a debut in franchise history with 35 – a mark previously held by LeBron James. He set the tone with a 21-point first half on a barrage of downhill drives and finishes at the rim, giving the Heat a legitimate Most Valuable Player candidate they haven’t had since James was on the roster. He played with pace and was practically impossible to guard in transition and in the paint, where he scored a game-high 24 points. Yet – and it’s essential to point out here that it’s merely one game and that it was always going to take some time for this group to find its potential – the Heat will be in trouble if they cannot do these two things. The Heat also got torched on defense, especially along the perimeter, which fed into the offensive struggles. Miami traded away much of its young core and had to scramble during the offseason to add worthy shooters. And on a team with Antetokounmpo as its centerpiece, shooting is a non-negotiable. Antetokounmpo carries so much gravity when he has the ball in his hands, sucking defenders into the paint, which tends to leave players wide open in the perimeter. It’s why Antetokounmpo has averaged at least 5.4 assists per game each of the last 10 seasons. Yet, Miami made only 8-of-33 attempts (24.2%) from 3-point range. Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Nikola Jović, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Pelle Larsson – players expected to convert catch-and-shoot looks – combined to go 3-of-20 (15%). “We didn’t get many good looks,” Heat coach Erik Spoelstra told reporters after the game. “(Antetokounmpo) was a force of nature, for sure, doing what he does. But we didn’t look like us offensively.” In fact, it was so bad for the Heat that Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who dropped 45 on Miami, actually made one more 3-pointer (nine total) than the entire Heat lineup. Spoelstra went on to say that Miami did “uncharacteristic” things, but he was generous with the good looks comment. A lot of them were with plenty of space. The issue was that role players seemingly still don’t know how to play with Antetokounmpo, with many resorting to standing around, waiting for the ball to come to them. Compounding the poor shooting was relative disinterest on defense. This is particularly uncharacteristic of Spoelstra and the Heat, who pride themselves on making everything difficult for opponents. Minnesota shot 46.9% from the field, which is fine – Miami was actually more efficient at 48.1% – but the Timberwolves unloaded from deep, draining 21-of-50 attempts (42%). The edge of converted 3-pointers for the Timberwolves, 13, created a differential of 39 points. Very few teams, if any, will be able to win with that disparity. The Heat under Spoelstra have usually had their defensive intensity feed offensive rhythm. Spoelstra’s teams do best when they get stops and force turnovers, so they can sprint out into transition. But when having to take the ball out time and time again, that momentum is totally neutralized. The good news for Antetokounmpo and the Heat is that it’s merely one of 82 and that they now know what they cannot let happen against a team that shoots well. For his part, Antetokounmpo chose to start the assessment from within, as he told reporters after the game, simply: “We have to trust what we’re doing.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves spoil Giannis' home debut with Heat

item.title: Bears get promising trade rumor on 17-sack veteran who once played in Chicago
item.description: Bears get promising trade rumor on 17-sack veteran who once played in Chicago originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the expectation that the Los Angeles Chargers will sell at the NFL trade deadline, the Chicago Bears are in a very interesting position to land some of those guys. Specifically, rumors suggest the Bears could be interested in Khalil Mack. Mack, an edge rusher who can get to the quarterback at a high level, is 35 and isn't the same player he once was. However, this Bears defense, which has proven above average despite its needs on that side of the ball, would only get better with a player of his caliber. Mack has proven himself throughout his long career, which began in 2014. That includes a 17-sack season for the Chargers in 2023. He also played for the Bears earlier in his career. According to the latest report, the Bears seem interested, though they still have a few things to figure out on their end. “The Bears got franchise quarterback Caleb Williams back from injury. They have a few weeks to see what that looks like before the deadline. But the unit clearly lacks bite and has been turnover-dependent and Mack is a player they know well from his time there,” Jason La Canfora wrote . With Caleb Williams back, the Bears are expected to be one of the top teams in the NFL, a squad with a chance to win a Super Bowl. Not that Mack guarantees anything, just as any other player traded at the deadline doesn't, but it makes Chicago a much better team, and that's what it has to do at this year's trade deadline. item.title: Tyrese Haliburton Makes Emotional Return as Pacers Defeat Pelicans
item.description: Photo by: Stephen Lew Tyrese Haliburton made his long-awaited return to regular-season NBA action Wednesday night, helping the Indiana Pacers defeat the New Orleans Pelicans 123-120 in their season opener. After missing the entire 2025-26 season with a torn Achilles tendon, the All Star point guard delivered a memorable performance that reminded fans what he can bring to Indiana. Haliburton finished with 23 points and 12 assists in 34 minutes, providing a major boost as the Pacers began their new campaign with a hard-fought road victory. His return came 486 days after he suffered the devastating injury during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Haliburton Delivers When It Matters Most While Haliburton showed some signs of rust throughout the game, he became increasingly comfortable as the night progressed. His passing helped create opportunities for his teammates, while his ability to attack the basket became especially important down the stretch. With the score tied at 116 in the fourth quarter, Haliburton drove past Trey Murphy III for a layup. He then attacked New Orleans again on the next possession, drawing a foul against defensive standout Herb Jones and completing a three point play. Those consecutive scoring possessions helped Indiana take control of a tight game and demonstrated Haliburton’s importance to the Pacers’ offense. Pascal Siakam led Indiana with 30 points, while Obi Toppin contributed 20 points off the bench. Andrew Nembhard added 18 points as the Pacers found enough offensive production to survive a competitive opener. An Emotional Moment After the Buzzer The victory meant more than just the first win of a new season. After the game, Haliburton became emotional during a postgame interview as he reflected on the long rehabilitation process and the challenges of being away from basketball. The injury occurred on the biggest stage of his career, ending his participation in the NBA Finals and forcing him to spend an entire season working toward his return. Seeing him back on the court, contributing to a victory and playing a decisive role late in the game represented a significant milestone for both Haliburton and the organization. A Promising Start for Indiana Haliburton’s return gives Indiana renewed optimism after a difficult season without its leading playmaker. His combination of scoring, passing and late-game decision-making could be crucial as the Pacers look to reestablish themselves in the Eastern Conference. Wednesday’s performance does not erase the challenges of returning from a serious injury, but it provides an encouraging first step. For Haliburton, the biggest victory was getting back to doing what he loves. For the Pacers, his return came with a win and a reminder of how dangerous this team can be with its star point guard back in the lineup.

item.title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone says something most New York fans won’t agree with
item.description: Yankees’ Aaron Boone says something most New York fans won’t agree with originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Many New York Yankees fans haven't been too happy with what Aaron Boone and Brian Cashman have done throughout much of their partnership, though it's also important to recognize that not everything is on either of their shoulders. The Yankees typically have a very talented roster from top to bottom with a chance to win a World Series. Unfortunately, that hasn't happened yet with Boone as the Yankees' skipper. Boone spoke to the media on Wednesday, offering insight into why his team hasn't done that yet and whether he believes he's the man to help New York do it. While it's not surprising to hear him say he believes he can manage a World Series team, Boone also understands that any answer he gives won't satisfy this fan base, which is looking for success. “Yeah. I mean we’ve got to prove that otherwise. Hopefully we are that bully and we’re the best team throughout the season next year and bully our way through the postseason,” Boone said , H/T Heavy. “But until we don’t I don’t have that answer for you. We have to answer that. Until the Brewers or Rays win a World Series they’ve never won a World Series. “I believe it can happen with me at the helm but any answer I give in defense of that isn’t going to be a great one or satisfy people. I think I’m good at my job, I think we have a lot of the right people in the building, but at the end of the day we haven’t won a championship with me at the helm and you know ultimately that’s what has to happen to satisfy certainly myself. That’s why I’m doing this… haven’t been able to do it yet.” Coaching in New York isn't easy, but being the skipper for the Yankees is even harder. A job in New York City already comes with a level of stress, and coaching the most historic organization in Major League Baseball only adds to that. Boone understands what it takes to win at this level because he played in New York back in the day, but he'll have to prove he can do it as a manager, too. item.title: “Men against kids”: Former Man United striker Dimitar Berbatov savages players after 4-1 humiliation by Como
item.description: “Men against kids”: Former Man United striker Dimitar Berbatov savages players after 4-1 humiliation by Como Manchester United suffered one of their most embarrassing results and performances in recent times on Wednesday evening. The match They were taken apart 4-1 by Italian side Como, and the truth is, it could have been more. The Serie A side were dominant in almost every metric and made a fool of United’s players and coaching staff on a dismal night in the Reds’ European history. United now find themselves seven matches without a win, with only three points from three matches in the Champions League phase. Dimitar Berbatov response Speaking to TNT Sports after the game, former Manchester United striker Dimitar Berbatov was far from impressed by what he saw. Reflecting on the match, he claimed, “it was a terrible, terrible night. A terrible game for United, nothing was happening, and Como outplayed them in every way possible. From the goals, from taking the ball, the possession, the confidence. Everything was there for Como.” Building further on his analysis, he explained, “it was like they were playing a second team. Look at the first goal, the confidence on the ball, the time on the ball.” The Bulgarian exclaimed that the result was one thing, but the performance was something else that needed to be assessed. He explained, “sometimes it’s not about the loss, it’s about how you lose, and today that was the point, how we lost that game of football. After a performance like this, probably, like every time, [people ask], ‘Are these the right players to compete on the highest stage? Is that the right manager? Is this the right way?'” Finally, Berbatov gave a damning assessment of the mindset of the current players at the club. He asserted, “today it didn’t look like everyone was giving their best on the pitch. Como looked like they were just having fun. It looked like men against kids.” United will have to respond against AFC Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon when they return to Old Trafford. item.title: Former Raptors star Serge Ibaka sends heartfelt message on Kawhi Leonard’s Toronto return
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images Former Raptors star Serge Ibaka sends heartfelt message on Kawhi Leonard’s Toronto return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kawhi Leonard ’s first regular-season game back with the Toronto Raptors brought back plenty of memories, and few people felt them more than Serge Ibaka. The former Raptors big man was at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday night as Leonard made his return to Toronto in a 135-92 rout of the Chicago Bulls . Speaking with Sportsnet during the game, Ibaka reflected on what it meant to see his 2019 championship teammate back in a Raptors uniform. “I think he always loved this place, you know. Sometimes we make decisions, you know, because of business side,” Ibaka said. “But I’m glad he realized, you know, Toronto is home for him. And he wants to come back here and to finish what he started here.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Watching him play here [again] on this court. There are so many beautiful memories." 🥹❤️ @sergeibaka joined @SNMichaud to chat about watching Kawhi's return to the Raptors. pic.twitter.com/XXjAg6vQlY — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) October 22, 2026 Ibaka admitted the night stirred up emotions from that title run. “Yes, so many memories,” Ibaka said. “Watching, sitting out there and watching him play here on this court. Yeah, bring so many beautiful memories.” Leonard famously left Toronto for the Los Angeles Clippers in free agency after leading the Raptors to the first championship in franchise history. Seven years later, he is back. Toronto agreed to acquire him in a June trade that sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and multiple draft picks to Los Angeles, though the deal was not finalized until September amid an NBA investigation into the Clippers . Leonard then signed a contract extension with the Raptors. Ibaka believes the situation mirrors what happened when Leonard first arrived in Toronto. “I think it’s kind of a little bit similar situation. Like when he came, you know, with us, it’s a new group,” Ibaka said. “These young guys, last year they had a great year. Adding Kawhi with them, I think they’re going to be a lot better this year.” Leonard backed that up in his return, scoring 23 points and going a perfect 11-of-11 from the free-throw line. Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley each added 23 points, while RJ Barrett chipped in 20 as Toronto never trailed. Ibaka also gave his approval to Barnes for keeping Leonard’s famous “What it do, baby” line alive. “I mean, I like that because he’s keeping that going,” Ibaka said. The Raptors will look to stay hot when they visit the Washington Wizards on Friday. Related: Kawhi Leonard sounds off on Raptors’ historic season opener Related: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard shares clear message to those waiting for his peak form

item.title: Zayden Lassiter welcomed to the 2027 Navy All-American Bowl
item.description: Long snapper Zayden Lassiter (Cochran, Georgia/ Bleckley County Academy) was officially honored as a 2027 Navy All-American during a virtual jersey presentation as part of the Road to the Dome tour. Navy All-American Bowl Long snapper Zayden Lassiter (Cochran, Georgia/ Bleckley County Academy) was officially honored as a 2027 Navy All-American during a virtual jersey presentation as part of the Road to the Dome tour. Latest Snapper Welcome @zlassiter24 to the 2027 Navy All-American Bowl @NBCSports #StingEm #NavyAAB @AmericasNavy pic.twitter.com/HzMrRfMH6S — Navy All-American Bowl (@AABonNBC) October 22, 2026 Lassiter will play in the annual East vs. West matchup inside the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday, January 9, 2027, live on NBC and Peacock, which marks the twenty-seventh anniversary of the event. The nationwide Road to the Dome tour will honor 100 Navy All-Americans with live and virtual jersey presentations. The series will be released weekly through social platforms across NBC Sports. Lassiter was selected by the Navy All-American Bowl Selection Committee, comprised of the All-American Bowl, Andrew Ivins (247Sports), Brandon Huffman (Rivals), and NXGN. Navy All-Americans are eligible for the Navy All-American Bowl Player of the Year Award, Anthony Muñoz Lineman of the Year Award, Navy All-American Bowl Defensive Player of the Year Award, Navy All-American Bowl Man of the Year, and Navy All-American Bowl Game MVP Award. About the All-American Bowl As an NBC Sports-owned property, the All-American Bowl is part of a marquee lineup of elite events that includes the Olympics and Paralympics, the NBA, WNBA, Major League Baseball, Notre Dame Football, the Premier League, and primetime’s #1 show for an unprecedented 15 consecutive years: Sunday Night Football . The All-American Bowl is annually the most-watched, most-talked about, and most-prestigious high school all-star event with more than four million unique television viewers and more than 25,000 fans in attendance. The history and tradition of the All-American Bowl is unparalleled, as it features: 665 draft picks; 110 Super Bowl champions; 300 Pro Bowl selections; and 18 Heisman finalists. For more information, visit nbcsports.com/college-football/navy-all-american-bowl or follow us on Facebook, X, and Instagram (@AABonNBC).

item.title: History comes home as St Louis City top Columbus Crew to win US Open Cup
item.description: Title is club’s first-ever since 2023 founding St Louis clubs have won 11 Open Cups all-time Daniel Edelman nets winner in 5-4 win on penalties For much of the 20th century, winning the US Open Cup required a team to beat someone from St Louis. The Gateway City was home to many of the nation’s best teams during some ramshackle eras of soccer in the United States, with six different clubs combining for 10 trophy lifts. The most recent came in 1988, when St Louis Busch Seniors beat San Francisco-based Greek-American AC in the last throes of a tournament history dominated by amateur and semi-pro teams. MLS has won every Open Cup but one since starting play in 1996, and St Louis didn’t have an MLS club until 2023. From the beginning, club figures spoke of aims to restore the city to soccer prominence. Well, mission accomplished. St Louis City are US Open Cup champions, outlasting the Columbus Crew 5-4 on penalties away from home to end the city’s 38-year wait for a major US soccer title and earn a place in the field for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal’s Declan Rice strikes late to deny Bayern Munich after Harry Kane penalty
item.description: It is as if Harry Kane cannot get enough of tormenting Arsenal. The Bayern Munich striker has plenty of form from his Tottenham days. He remains the top scorer in north London derby history with 14 goals. He made an impact yet again here and yet it was not a night when he had the final word. That honour fell to Declan Rice, the Arsenal midfielder storming into the Bayern area in the 82nd minute to guide home a low finish that Kane would have been proud to call his own. Arsenal were hunting their latest statement result. Only once had they ever won away against Bayern – the 2-0 in the Champions League last 16 second leg in 2013, although it did not prevent an away goals exit. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player that night. When Eberechi Eze, who came on for the injured Bukayo Saka in the 10th minute, gave them the lead midway through the first half, their hopes surged. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Taha Hashim
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta has mastered the art of making substitutions at Arsenal
item.description: Arsenal have beaten Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Leeds this season thanks to goals from players off the bench By Opta Analyst They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern. After Mikel Arteta’s substitutes proved decisive yet again for Arsenal, we can say with certainty that his ability to change games from his bench is a pattern worth noting. With Arsenal labouring away at Nottingham Forest and the game drifting towards a goalless draw, Noni Madueke – introduced at half-time – won the game for the visitors , shimmying inside and striking a heavily deflected right-footed shot past Matz Sels. It was hardly a glamorous goal but it secured three valuable Premier League points for Arteta’s side. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country
item.description: Female players including Carlinha and Tayla Carolina have spoken out against the far right, who they fear will harm the women’s game as well as wider society The day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title. It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people. Continue reading...

item.title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
item.description: Peta calls on club to never again use a live animal mascot ‘There’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a stadium’ A leading animal rights group has urged Crystal Palace to retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk. In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.description: Wiegman says she ‘cannot think of a better job in football’ She can target three European titles in row with Lionesses Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row. Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up. item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
